//: Slither configuration for AgentPay's audit gate (build brief M8:
EVERY exclusion below is a deliberate, reviewed decision — not a way to make
the build green. Each detector class is justified here and in
docs/SECURITY_NOTES.md, with the full findings table in HANDOFF.md.
Findings that were REAL were fixed, not excluded:
ICrossChainSpendRouter, so the compiler enforces the contract AgentWallet
depends on (verified: drifting the interface now fails the build).
- reentrancy-events: ccipReceive now emits before its external calls
Mocks are test scaffolding and are filtered out entirely.

timestamp: 10 findings, all intentional. Every time window in this system is measured
in HOURS or DAYS: the daily budget day-bucket (86400s), the staking unstake
cooldown and settlement dispute window (= governance disputeWindow), the
ScoreRegistry commit/reveal windows, and the oracle staleness bound.
A miner can nudge block.timestamp by seconds; against an hours-to-days
window that is immaterial. Worst case at a day boundary: an agent's daily
budget resets a few seconds early. Bounded, and accepted by the brief's
incorrect-equality: (a) AgentWallet day-bucket comparisons (`today == currentDay`, x3): equality
on an integer DAY INDEX is precisely the intended semantic - 'is this
the same day bucket'. There is no balance to manipulate here.
credit() rejects a zero amount (ZeroAmount), so 0 unambiguously means
'no such payment'. That invariant is enforced and tested.
unused-return: (a) PriceFeedAdapter.latestUsdPrice: Slither noise. We DO consume roundId,
answer, updatedAt and answeredInRound; only `startedAt` is skipped in the
tuple destructure, which is what trips the detector.
(b) AgentWallet.spend discards routeSpend's returned CCIP messageId. Not a
the SAME transaction, so the cross-chain audit handle is already on-chain
and correlates by tx hash. Storing it twice would only add gas.
missing-zero-check: 2 findings on AgentWallet's `agent` operator, both intentional.
Setting agent = address(0) is the documented way to CLEAR the operator
(see setAgent's NatSpec: 'Appoint (or clear)'). It is safe because
msg.sender can never be address(0) in a real transaction, so a zero agent
simply means 'only the owner may spend'.
low-level-calls: withdrawNative. This is the RECOMMENDED way to transfer native ETH (transfer
/send forward a fixed 2300 gas and break on contract recipients). The return
value IS checked and the function is onlyOwner.
naming-convention: _treasury, ...). This is the standard Solidity convention for a parameter
that shadows a state variable, is used consistently across the codebase, and
matches OpenZeppelin's own style. Slither prefers plain mixedCase.
unindexed-event-address: events read by scanning a single contract's full history, not by filtering on
an address topic, so an index would add cost without a consumer.
solc-version: Excluded because the compiler is PINNED to 0.8.24 by the course toolchain
(build brief section 2.5). Slither recommends a newer patch release; pinning
